sections.description: This section describes the patient’s presenting symptoms, vital signs, physical findings, and the initial obstetric and systemic evaluation that guided the diagnostic pathway.
subtopics: Patient demographics and obstetric history (nulliparous, age, BMI, gestational age)
Chief complaints: upper left quadrant abdominal pain, pelvic pain, dyspnoea
Physical examination: abdominal enlargement, tender subphrenic mass, bimanual pelvic findings
Baseline vital signs and respiratory status
Initial laboratory data: anaemia, inflammatory markers, urine culture (Klebsiella), COVID‑19 test
Initial pain management and positional therapy
Importance of a multidisciplinary triage (emergency, obstetrics, radiology, surgery)

sections.section_title: 2. Diagnostic Work‑up and Formulation of the Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: Focuses on the step‑wise imaging and laboratory investigations, interpretation of findings, and construction of a differential diagnosis specific to large abdominal/pelvic masses in pregnancy.
subtopics: Ultrasound findings: size, location, cystic nature, vascularisation, relation to uterus
Role of colour‑Doppler in distinguishing pedunculated leiomyoma vs ovarian lesion
Serum tumour markers in pregnancy: CA‑125 physiology, trends, and limitations
Non‑contrast MRI protocol in the second trimester: safety considerations, sequences used, and key imaging characteristics (wall thickness, T1/T2 signal, solid components)
Differential diagnoses:
• Decidualised endometrioma
• Cystic degeneration of a uterine leiomyoma
• Primary ovarian cystic tumor (benign vs malignant)
• Hydropic degeneration or necrosis of a pedunculated myoma
Interpretation of imaging‑clinical discordance (upper mass appeared ovarian, lower mass contiguous with uterus)
Decision points that prompted surgical exploration (size >10 cm, pain, dyspnoea, risk of torsion/rupture, inconclusive imaging)

sections.description: Explains the multidisciplinary consensus process, operative planning, intra‑operative findings, and specific technical steps taken to treat the symptomatic mass while preserving pregnancy.
subtopics: Indications for surgery during pregnancy: symptomatic, rapidly enlarging, torsion, suspected necrosis, maternal respiratory compromise
Risk–benefit analysis: fetal viability, gestational age, estimated blood loss, need for uterus‑preserving technique
Choice of approach: laparotomy vs laparoscopy – rationale for open longitudinal xipho‑pubic incision at 21 weeks + 6 days
Pre‑operative preparation:
• Informed consent specific to maternal‑fetal risks
• Prophylactic antibiotics (cefazolin + clarithromycin based on culture)
• Progesterone supplementation protocol (intramuscular 100 mg pre‑ and post‑op, then caproate hydroxyprogesterone)
Intra‑operative sequence:
• Peritoneal fluid sampling for cytology and culture
• Confirmation of fetal heart activity
• Identification and excision of the pedunculated cranial leiomyoma (double‑clamp technique, hemostasis, uterine wall closure)
• Decision to leave the caudal mass in situ – obstetric safety considerations
• Estimated operative time, blood loss, and intra‑operative fetal monitoring
Post‑operative immediate care: analgesia, monitoring for uterine contractility, continuation of progesterone, antibiotic course

sections.section_title: 4. Obstetric Follow‑up, Delivery Planning, and Post‑operative Outcomes
sections.description: Covers the maternal recovery, obstetric surveillance, delivery strategy, and neonatal results, as well as the handling of residual myoma.
subtopics: Management of postoperative anaemia: iron infusion, blood transfusion thresholds
Serial obstetric ultrasounds: fetal growth percentile, amniotic fluid index, myoma size monitoring
Resolution of the caudal myoma size postpartum (partial regression to 7.5 cm)
Decision for elective caesarean section at 37 weeks on the previous laparotomy scar – rationale (obstructive pelvic mass, scar integrity)
Neonatal outcomes: Apgar scores, birth weight, immediate postpartum adaptation
Long‑term follow‑up plan: surveillance of residual leiomyoma, counseling regarding future surgical removal, impact on fertility
Pathology report: benign leiomyoma with ischemic necrosis, no malignancy

sections.section_title: 5. Clinical Pearls, Evidence Synthesis, and Guideline Implications
sections.description: Summarizes the key teaching points, integrates current literature on myoma management in pregnancy, and proposes practical algorithms for similar cases.
subtopics: Epidemiology of uterine leiomyomas and adnexal masses in pregnancy
Diagnostic algorithm for large pelvic masses in pregnant patients (step‑wise US → non‑contrast MRI → tumour markers → multidisciplinary review)
Interpretation of CA‑125 trends in pregnancy and its limited specificity
Safety profile of non‑contrast MRI after the first trimester (≤1.5 T, no gadolinium)
When to consider myomectomy during pregnancy: size >10 cm, pedunculated with torsion, refractory symptoms, or impending obstetric compromise
Comparison of laparotomy vs laparoscopic myomectomy outcomes in second‑trimester surgery
Progesterone prophylaxis to reduce risk of preterm labour during intra‑operative fetal monitoring
Algorithm for delivery planning in the presence of residual uterine masses (vaginal delivery vs elective CS)
Future research gaps: randomized data on timing of myomectomy, optimal imaging protocols, and long‑term reproductive outcomes
